Q1:

library(mclust)
## Package 'mclust' version 6.1.2
## Type 'citation("mclust")' for citing this R package in publications.
data_lu4 <- read.delim("LU-4.snv.txt", header=TRUE)
head(data_lu4)
##   X.CHROM     POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER                   INFO t_alt_count
## 1       1  249208  .   C   T    .   PASS Callers=mutect,strelka          40
## 2       1 1005912  .   T   A    .   PASS Callers=mutect,strelka          42
## 3       1 2822140  .   C   T    .   PASS Callers=mutect,strelka          18
## 4       1 4135793  .   C   G    .   PASS Callers=mutect,strelka          27
## 5       1 4499985  .   C   A    .   PASS Callers=mutect,strelka          31
## 6       1 4671564  .   A   T    .   PASS Callers=mutect,strelka          41
##   t_ref_count                                 X X.1
## 1         128 Variant_Classification=intergenic    
## 2          99 Variant_Classification=intergenic    
## 3         133 Variant_Classification=intergenic    
## 4          95 Variant_Classification=intergenic    
## 5         119 Variant_Classification=intergenic    
## 6          99 Variant_Classification=intergenic
data_lu4$vaf <- data_lu4$t_alt_count / (data_lu4$t_alt_count + data_lu4$t_ref_count)

dim(data_lu4)
## [1] 4207   13
hist(data_lu4$vaf,
     breaks = 50,
     main = "VAF Distribution for LU-4 Tumor Sample",
     xlab = "Variant Allele Frequency")

#There is a  peak at a low VAF range (~0.05 - 0.1). This shows a large number of subclonal mutations that likely occured later during tumor evolution and are present in only a fraction of the cancer cells.
#There is another wider peak around VAF ~0.25 - 0.3. This likely represents the major clone of the tumor. The shift from the expected 0.5 VAF suggests either low tumor purity or specific copy number alterations(CNA) affecting these sites.There is another possibility, that this peak is a combination of two subclones merged together.

# ******** The mclust results from Q2 confirm that the wide peak observed is  a merger of multiple clusters. While the initial visual analysis suggested two peaks, further data analysis proves the existence of four distinct cell populations. Specifically, Cluster 3 (VAF ~0.24) and Cluster 4 (VAF ~0.44) explain the previously noted "shift" and width of the peak(it represents a complex clonal structure rather than a single population).

Q2:

mod_lu4 <- densityMclust(data_lu4$vaf)

summary(mod_lu4)
## ------------------------------------------------------- 
## Density estimation via Gaussian finite mixture modeling 
## ------------------------------------------------------- 
## 
## Mclust V (univariate, unequal variance) model with 4 components: 
## 
##  log-likelihood    n df      BIC      ICL
##        3816.089 4207 11 7540.388 6367.125
#mathematical validation of the model
plot(mod_lu4, what = "diagnostic", type = "cdf")

plot(mod_lu4, what = "diagnostic", type = "qq")

#The close overlap between the two lines in the CDF plot shows that the model accurately captures the overall distribution of the mutation data.
#Alignment of points along the line in the Q–Q plot indicates a good fit of the model.


#Dimension Reduction
mod_lu4dr <- MclustDR(mod_lu4)

summary(mod_lu4dr)
## ----------------------------------------------------------------- 
## Dimension reduction for model-based clustering and classification 
## ----------------------------------------------------------------- 
## 
## Mixture model type: Mclust (V, 4) 
##         
## Clusters    n
##        1  619
##        2  600
##        3 2823
##        4  165
## 
## Estimated basis vectors: 
##              Dir1
## data_lu4$vaf    1
## 
##                  Dir1
## Eigenvalues   0.88284
## Cum. %      100.00000
cluster_means <- mod_lu4dr$mu
print(cluster_means)
##            [,1]       [,2]      [,3]      [,4]
## [1,] 0.05826428 0.08932871 0.2421087 0.4472558
plot(mod_lu4dr, what = "classification")

#the cluster separation within the reduced-dimension space

plot(mod_lu4dr, what = "density")

summary_table <- data.frame(
  Cluster_ID = c("Cluster 4", "Cluster 3", "Cluster 2", "Cluster 1"),
  Size = c(165, 2823, 595, 624),
  Mean_VAF = c(0.447, 0.242, 0.089, 0.058)
)


trunk_vaf <- max(summary_table$Mean_VAF)

summary_table$Scaled_Mean_VAF<- summary_table$Mean_VAF / trunk_vaf

summary_table$Estimated_CCF_Percent <- summary_table$Scaled_Mean_VAF* 100

summary_table$Status <- c("Founder / Trunk Clone(Purity Anchor", 
                          "Dominant Subclone", 
                          "Subclone", 
                          "Subclone")
summary_table$Zygosity <- "Heterozygous"

print(summary_table)
##   Cluster_ID Size Mean_VAF Scaled_Mean_VAF Estimated_CCF_Percent
## 1  Cluster 4  165    0.447       1.0000000             100.00000
## 2  Cluster 3 2823    0.242       0.5413870              54.13870
## 3  Cluster 2  595    0.089       0.1991051              19.91051
## 4  Cluster 1  624    0.058       0.1297539              12.97539
##                                Status     Zygosity
## 1 Founder / Trunk Clone(Purity Anchor Heterozygous
## 2                   Dominant Subclone Heterozygous
## 3                            Subclone Heterozygous
## 4                            Subclone Heterozygous
cat("Number of clusters identified (G):", mod_lu4$G, "\n") 
## Number of clusters identified (G): 4
#VAF values were scaled to estimate the Cancer Cell Fraction (CCF). By normalizing the Mean VAF of each cluster to the founding trunk (Cluster 4), Now the clonal mutations represent 100% of the cancer cell population.Instead of scaling I could just do this: VAF*2 , but it is not as accurate as scaling ( becuase by scaling we remove non-cancer cells, so ccf would be 100% for the trunk population)
# G= 4
#In the analysis of tumor LU-4, all four  clusters are considered heterozygous. This assumption is based on cluster 4 (trunk), which has a VAF of 0.447 , consistent with heterozygous mutations in a high-purity tumor. Clusters 3, 2, and 1, with lower VAFs (0.24, 0.09, and 0.06, respectively), follow the same pattern and represent subclonal branches present in only a fraction of the cellular population. In the absence of local copy-number and purity data, all mutated regions are assumed to be diploid.The assumption fully consistent with the cluster distribution inferred by the mclust model.

َQ3: file name: Q3.pdf

data_c1 <- data_lu4[which(mod_lu4$classification == 1),]
data_c2 <- data_lu4[which(mod_lu4$classification == 2),]
data_c3 <- data_lu4[which(mod_lu4$classification == 3),]
data_c4 <- data_lu4[which(mod_lu4$classification == 4),]

cat("Cluster 4 (Trunk) Mean VAF:", mean(data_c4$vaf), "\n")
## Cluster 4 (Trunk) Mean VAF: 0.5073195
cat("Cluster 3 (Major) Mean VAF:", mean(data_c3$vaf), "\n")
## Cluster 3 (Major) Mean VAF: 0.2489266
cat("Cluster 2 (Subclone) Mean VAF:", mean(data_c2$vaf), "\n")
## Cluster 2 (Subclone) Mean VAF: 0.09312967
cat("Cluster 1 (Subclone) Mean VAF:", mean(data_c1$vaf), "\n")
## Cluster 1 (Subclone) Mean VAF: 0.05643398
stats_summary <- data.frame(
  Cluster = c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4"),
  Mean_VAF = c(mean(data_c1$vaf), mean(data_c2$vaf), mean(data_c3$vaf), mean(data_c4$vaf)),
  Median_VAF = c(median(data_c1$vaf), median(data_c2$vaf), median(data_c3$vaf), median(data_c4$vaf))
)

print(stats_summary)
##   Cluster   Mean_VAF Median_VAF
## 1      C1 0.05643398 0.05645161
## 2      C2 0.09312967 0.09090909
## 3      C3 0.24892659 0.24822695
## 4      C4 0.50731950 0.48760331
#The proximity between Mean and Median values across all clusters confirms a symmetrical distribution of mutations within each subclone.



# Extract cluster proportions (representing the thickness/width of the evolutionary branches)
cluster_props <- prop.table(table(mod_lu4$classification))
names(cluster_props) <- c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4")

barplot(cluster_props, 
        main="Clonal Proportions for Evolutionary Tree",
        col=c("lightblue", "lightgreen", "coral", "gold"),
        ylab="Proportion of total mutations")

plot(data_sp4$VAF_LN1, data_sp4$VAF_LN2,
     xlab="VAF in LN1 (%)", 
     ylab="VAF in LN2 (%)",
     main="VAF Correlation between SP4 LN1 and LN2"
     )

#Reference Line for recognising mutations with same VAF in LN1 and LN2
abline(0, 1)

#Clonal/Shared Mutations: A significant number of mutations cluster along the reference line, indicating they have similar VAF values in both LN1 and LN2. These are shared clonal mutations that likely formed the "trunk" of the tumor before it spread to different lymph nodes.

# Several mutations deviate significantly from the reference line or are positioned along the axes (VAF > 0 in one sample but ~0 in the other). This indicates private mutations or subclonal populations that are unique to either LN1 or LN2, reflecting divergent evolution and heterogeneity between the two metastatic sites.

Q5:

BIC_sp4 <- mclustBIC(data_sp4_vaf)
plot(BIC_sp4)

summary(BIC_sp4)
## Best BIC values:
##              VVV,4        VVV,3        VVV,5
## BIC      -1743.766 -1746.335837 -1753.259975
## BIC diff     0.000    -2.570214    -9.494352
mod_sp4 <- Mclust(data_sp4_vaf, x = BIC_sp4)
summary(mod_sp4, parameters = T)
